claims: For valid sign-extended 32-bit inputs, Sony's EE manual defines MULT as a signed 32-bit product and specifies the low and high 32-bit halves in LO and HI; each 64-bit destination contains its corresponding 32-bit half sign-extended.

For valid sign-extended 32-bit inputs, Sony's EE manual defines MULTU using unsigned low-32-bit operands, while specifying sign-extended 32-bit result halves in LO and HI; the listed operation also writes the low half to GPR[rd].
Sony's EE manual defines MULT1 as the signed word product written to LO1 and HI1, with the low half also written to GPR[rd], and the product halves sign-extended.

Sony's EE manual defines MADD as a signed 32-bit product added to the concatenation of the low 32 bits of HI and LO; the result's low and high words are sign-extended into LO, HI, and the low word is written to GPR[rd].

The pinned PS2Recomp revision emits a destination-nonzero branch and a destination-zero branch for each of the four audited operations; MULT1 uses the secondary hi1/lo1 bank, and the MADD template reads the low 32 bits of HI and LO for its accumulator.
The saved historical static export contains 241 MULT, 5 MULTU, 24 MULT1, and 3 MADD instructions at distinct addresses.

The source-extracted native probe compared all eight actual emitted branches against an independent widened/modulo oracle for 201440 synthetic checks each, with zero mismatches; a deliberately corrupted destination-bank mutant produced 201440 mismatches for each branch.

evidence.text: Sony Computer Entertainment, EE Core Instruction Set Manual Version 6.0, printed p.154 MULT: signed 32-bit product; LO63..0=(prod31)32||prod31..0; HI63..0=(prod63)32||prod63..32; GPR[rd]63..0=(prod31)32||prod31..0. Operands must be sign-extended 32-bit values; no arithmetic exception; omitted rd is zero. Printed p.156 MULTU: product = (0||GPR[rs]31..0) x (0||GPR[rt]31..0); LO and HI each get a sign-extended result word, and GPR[rd] gets the sign-extended low word. Printed p.155 MULT1: signed product with LO1, HI1, and GPR[rd] receiving sign-extended low/high words. Printed p.142 MADD: signed word product plus (HI31..0||LO31..0); LO and HI get sign-extended result words; GPR[rd] gets sign-extended low word. Source PDF SHA-256 104205afc6f5a5071168d8bf693a6c8b4db9a02e1aa66eb51a828e8951f5c069. Extracted manual pages were previously Jev-screened for injection/relevance, pass.

Pinned PS2Recomp commit c5a9d02573410a2085a4b4b831b0b68ba3515440. Exact source hashes: ps2xRuntime/include/ps2_runtime_macros.h c0dfe8104803a380ff4f38a3ba3d5ed1979c68ad7234d83230863f079f354c4e; ps2xRecomp/src/lib/special_translator.cpp 98adc0305effdd57ca34ea029070f117379bd7e78c9f8944a8e9276c8c7bd3cd; ps2xRecomp/src/lib/mmi_translator.cpp 24deb4f0bc0004c42674e0340d80e50e6e676b326f11d6a2df3dd0b60319249f. Extracted actual templates: MULT and MULTU write ctx->lo and ctx->hi, with rd variants calling SET_GPR_S32; zero-rd variants omit that write. MULT1 similarly writes ctx->lo1 and ctx->hi1. MADD computes Ps2HiLoToU64(ctx->hi,ctx->lo), signed GPR_S32 product, adds, writes sign-extended words to lo/hi and low to rd in the rd branch. The header helper Ps2HiLoToU64 masks each argument to low 32 bits before composing the accumulator.

Pinned static export SHA-256 554f29697a3569e10b466e18caea5260d96b5a3a8741b586d811fa26beaa6383, executable SHA-256 216711210898aee296eed73d0776e7f733bac04c334002683bce769c86beea95, language r5900:LE:32:default, 3446 functions. Exact unique instruction counts by first mnemonic token: MULT 241; MULTU 5; MULT1 24; MADD 3. Per-op ordered address list SHA-256: MULT 7d6e5b1738872ae65198d1adf57181a4a4b6f5d2aacd32b9537a1d3e41429c19; MULTU bd728079c12bb6c3226ba531692e74316d12071269f4b039982df620bda42e; MULT1 0fbb839095c73977ecce58819abc6cf3cf3ed48c9f515e038503f3694191fb12; MADD 992a189836187425ad71f297ec285cd76cd75a7d5c15dac57221d8e7fde0a03f.

The source-pinned verifier compiled wrappers containing actual extracted PS2Recomp production templates and pinned runtime helpers with clang++ C++20 and -fsanitize=undefined. The independent oracle uses widened signed/unsigned multiplication and modulo-2^64 accumulator addition. For each of eight extracted branches, result.json reports 201440 checks and zero mismatches. A negative-control build flips the selected HI/LO low-bank bit; it reports 201440 mismatches for each branch. Tests used 12x12 directed edge pairs plus 20000 deterministic random input pairs, across ten register modes (distinct operands, rd aliasing each input, same sources, all alias, source register zero, both source registers zero, rd zero, and rd zero with aliased sources). Output checks include preserved non-output registers, upper 64-bit register halves, register zero, and untouched alternate accumulator bank. No original game routine or emulator was executed; this is not silicon equivalence or timing/interlock validation.
